Adding gSpeech to your Main Menu. You have two options you can add it to the ~/.local/share/applications/ directory so that it is just added for the current user or if you would like it to be added for all users you can add it to /usr/share/applications/ , I will use adding it for all users as the example. 

cd /usr/share/applications
touch gSpeech.desktop
vim gSpeech.desktop

Add the following lines to the file, note you will need to change USER to your username.

[Desktop Entry]
Encoding=UTF-8
Version=1.0
Type=Application
Terminal=false
Exec=/home/USER/gSpeech/gSpeech.sh
Name=gSpeech
Icon=/home/USER/gSpeech/icons/gSpeech.svg
GenericName=TTS
Categories=AudioVideo;

That is it, it will now show up in your audio video section of your main menu. Also, since it resides in the notification area and it nice to have there, so I also added it to the startup applications list. Let me know if you have any questions.

Also, if you are not familiar with vim, I suggest using vimtutor, vim and vi are the shit once you get familiar with them. Of course you can use gedit or whatever other editor you want to create gSpeech.desktop
